hourly.summary: Arsenal scraped a nervy 2-1 win at Slavia Prague thanks to a blistering first half from Madueke and Gyokeres, but a second-half capitulation nearly cost them three points. Fans are relieved to extend the unbeaten European away run to 10, but the mood is dominated by dread at the upcoming fixture congestion—Dortmund, Man City, Spurs, and Real Madrid all loom in a dizzying November-December gauntlet. The refrain "put teams to the sword" remains a desperate wish rather than reality.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment remained consistently positive throughout the day, anchored by the statement 1-0 win at Anfield that sent them top of the Premier League. The mood evolved from early-morning buzzing confidence into midday buoyancy as William Saliba returned to training, culminating in hopeful anticipation for his Champions League comeback against Slavia Prague. Across all summaries, quiet confidence in the squad's depth and title credentials dominates, with only minor tactical debates and banter tempering the optimism.

weekly.summary: The week began with optimism but plunged into crisis after a humiliating Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town, sustaining days of embarrassment and anxious dread ahead of the Anfield clash before culminating in a historic, euphoric 1-0 victory at Liverpool that sent Arsenal top of the table and completed a dramatic emotional redemption. The arc traces a sharp V-shape from pride through embarrassment to triumph. Dominant themes: cup humiliation, Anfield hoodoo anxiety, and ultimate villain-arc conquest.
